\label{sec:phase-seg}

We segment each generated sequence into three \emph{reasoning phases} based on the local attention sparsity of each token position. For each query position $i$, we compute per-head sparsity as the fraction of attention weights falling below $0.01 \times \max_j a_{i,h,j}$, then average across heads to obtain a scalar sparsity value per position. The resulting sparsity trajectory is partitioned into terciles via quantile boundaries: \emph{low-sparsity} (bottom third, corresponding to diffuse attention during exploratory reasoning), \emph{mid-sparsity}, and \emph{high-sparsity} (top third, corresponding to focused attention during structured computation). Contiguous segments shorter than $\texttt{min\_phase\_length}=10$ tokens are merged into adjacent phases to suppress noise.

\label{sec:stats}

All confidence intervals and significance tests are computed via the nonparametric bootstrap with $B = 10{,}000$ resamples \cite{efron1993bootstrap}.
